title: Probabilistic semantics of the final test
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $os$ be a Boolean, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $n,\ell,S,K,B,\mathrm{cnt},c,d$ be natural numbers. Suppose $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le B$, $\mathrm{cnt}\le K+1$, and $c,d\le K$. Then the final-test configuration, initialized with register values $(n,\ell,S,K,0,\mathrm{cnt},c,d,0)$, has probabilistic semantics with probability $1$ if the decision rule is true and probability $0$ otherwise; that rule is $1\le\mathrm{cnt}$ when $os$ is true, and $K+1<2\mathrm{cnt}$ when $os$ is false.
replaced:
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean word,
and let $n,\ell,S,K,B,\mathrm{cnt},c,d$ be natural numbers. Suppose $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le
B$, $\mathrm{cnt}\le K+1$, and $c,d\le K$. Then the final-test configuration with the
register tuple initialized from $(n,\ell,S,K,0,\mathrm{cnt},c,d,0)$ has probabilistic
semantics with probability $1$ when $os$ is true and $\mathrm{cnt}\ge1$, or when $os$ is
false and $K+1<2\mathrm{cnt}$; otherwise it has probability $0$.
